title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey, November 2026 — the New York Fed's half of the pair, printing on the closing Monday of the Philadelphia Fed's collection window
source: EST: TWO NEW YORK FED PRIMARIES AGREE ON MONDAY 2026-11-16, 08:30 ET, fetched direct 2026-11-05 (HTTP 200 each). (1) newyorkfed.org/survey/empire/empiresurvey_overview (132,035 bytes): its 2026 release table renders 'SEP 15 · OCT 15 · NOV 16 · DEC 15' with 'Released at or shortly after 8:30 a.m.' beneath it. (2) newyorkfed.org/research/calendars/nationalecon_cal (111,963 bytes): the November grid lists 'Empire State Manufacturing Survey (08:30)' on the 16th, the next dated entry after 'Producer Price Index (PPI)' on the 13th. Weekday arithmetic agrees: the 15th is a Sunday, and the page's own pattern (Feb 15 and Aug 15 2026 were weekend days and printed Feb 17 and Aug 17) rolls forward to Monday the 16th. Filed estimate on the same taxonomy count as the Empire 09-15, 10-15 and 12-15 entries had before #3117's FRB: prefix; a proposal can never be confirmed, so the owner's first session decides whether to promote it. notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the philly-fed-mfg-2026-11-19 D-14 pulse, 2026-11-05. This is the entry its 2026-09-10 initial research DECLINED (decline (a)) only because it could not reach a primary date: that session read the overview page as text and found the collection rule but no 2026 dates, because the release table renders as bare month and day tokens. Read as the rendered table, and cross-checked against the NY Fed's own national economic calendar, the date is on two primaries. Why it earns a file: (1) it is the missing November half of the Empire-Philly pair that the 10-15 and 12-17 Philly ledgers are built on (Empire 09-15, 10-15 and 12-15 all exist; 11-16 does not). (2) 11-16 is the closing Monday of the Philadelphia Fed's own November collection window (11-09 to 11-16), so the two surveys' November readings overlap in time. (3) It prints alone at 08:30 on a day with no other tracked release in that slot (unlike 10-15, which shared it with retail sales and PPI), but weekly initial jobless claims do not fall on a Monday, so the slot is genuinely clean. Inside the horizon: 11 days out, low impact, within allImpactsWithinDays 30.
